title: AI Hallucinations in State Farm Insurance Outside Lawyers' Filings

reading.body:
This is a model hallucination failure occurring at the point of legal document preparation. An AI tool called Irys, used by outside defense counsel, generated case citations, case titles, and quoted text that did not exist, and those fabrications were submitted across multiple court filings without being verified against actual legal databases before filing. The failure is one of a system asserting false information as fact, combined with a deployment that lacked a human verification step capable of catching invented citations.

The failure happened after the output left the model and before it entered the court record, which is precisely the gap where a cite-checking step, whether manual or automated against a verified legal database, would have caught it. The same failure type has appeared in other documented cases in the United States and elsewhere, and the pattern is consistent: generative AI produces plausible-looking but nonexistent legal authority, and no one confirms existence before submission.

What is not established is whether the AI tool itself was marketed or designed for legal citation work, whether the lawyers knew the citations were unverified at the time of filing, and no court finding of sanctionable conduct in this specific matter has been reported in the available sources.

reports.title: State Farm defense lawyers admit AI generated fake cases in LA lawsuit
AI hallucinated case law in insurance company’s filings in L.A. County house fire dispute
AI Hallucinations in State Farm Insurance Outside Lawyers' Filings

summary:
# Summary

State Farm's defense lawyers in a Los Angeles lawsuit apologized for using artificial intelligence that generated fake legal cases and non-existent quotes in their court filings. The homeowner, Fa'alagilagi Meni-Siliga, sued State Farm and others after a 2020 fire left her Carson home uninhabitable, followed by water damage during repairs. When delays prevented completion of the work, she lost her home to foreclosure and declared bankruptcy. The lawyer who used the AI tool called Irys confirmed that seven case citations across eight filings did not exist, along with incorrect case titles and fabricated quotes.

The incident highlights a growing problem in the legal profession, with 41 percent of law firms now using generative AI. A Paris-based researcher has documented nearly 1,900 cases of legal hallucinations worldwide, mostly in the United States. Last year, a California attorney received a record ten-thousand-dollar fine for using ChatGPT in a brief containing twenty-one fake quotes. Meni-Siliga's case is scheduled to proceed to trial in October, and State Farm said it expects its lawyers to maintain the highest ethical standards.
